bugs: UserObserver only handles team_id changes on update. wasChanged() is false on create, so a user created straight into a team isn't counted. Probe confirmed: members_count stayed 1 after a new teammate was created, and it stays stale for the full 300s TTL (app/Observers/UserObserver.php:13-16).

Dashboard doesn't do stale-while-revalidate. On every miss or invalidation, concurrent readers block on the lock for up to 5s instead of getting stale data straight away. If a cold cache has no ':last' entry, each waiter that times out runs the expensive build itself (TeamDashboardCache.php:31-36), which is a stampede on the path that's meant to protect against one.
Marking a task done without completed_at isn't counted in tasks_completed_last_7_days. Probe: status=done with no timestamp gave 0. Nothing in the model or observer keeps the two fields consistent.
antipatterns: app/Services/TeamDashboardCache.php:20-38: a hand-rolled lock, versioned key and ':last' fallback where Cache::flexible covers the 'stale up to 5 min' requirement
app/Services/TeamDashboardCache.php:17 and app/Services/ExchangeRates.php:21: primitive int $lockWaitSeconds constructor parameters added only as test seams
bootstrap/app.php:20-24: adds EncryptCookies/StartSession to the api middleware group, which the task doesn't need
app/Models/Task.php:53-56: a forTeam whereIn-subquery scope where a Team::tasks() hasManyThrough relation would do; the Team model has no tasks relation
app/Services/BuildTeamDashboard.php:17-18: raw where('team_id') queries instead of going through Team relations
app/Services/TeamDashboardCache.php:59-67: Cache::add plus get on every read to mint a random version
strengths: Thorough, fast Pest suite (43 tests): datasets for each kind of invalidation, a mid-computation invalidation race test, lock contention without real sleeps, and travel() for TTL boundaries
Invalidates on member join/leave through a UserObserver, and handles projects or tasks moving between teams
The HTTP client is split out and well configured: baseUrl, acceptJson, connectTimeout, a timeout from config, throw(), a check for malformed bodies and report($e)
Thin controllers using the `?? abort()` idiom; the FormRequest normalises the code to upper case and validates alpha:ascii plus size:3
Exchange rates use a lock with a double-checked read, a failure backoff and a 30-day last-known copy, all well tested

bugs: Member changes aren't invalidated because there's no User observer. A new teammate stays out of member_count until the 60s flexible fresh window expires. Probe confirmed it. This is minor: the task only requires projects and tasks to be reflected within seconds, and the staleness is bounded.
antipatterns: app/Support/FetchExchangeRates.php:85: Log::warning with a string message instead of report($e), which loses the exception context
app/Support/FetchExchangeRates.php:15-25: the timeout and TTLs are hard-coded constants while the URL comes from config; there's no connectTimeout
app/Observers/TaskObserver.php:15-21: the completed_at domain rule sits in an observer whose main job is cache invalidation (and which is after-commit)
tests/Feature/ExchangeRatesTest.php:117-129: the lock-contention test really blocks for 4s because the wait time can't be configured
tests/Feature/DashboardTest.php:77: uses the DB facade without importing it (works only through the global alias)
strengths: Cache::flexible([60, 300]) is exactly what the requirement asks for (serve stale for up to 5 min, refresh in the background), and a versioned key means a recompute that started before a write is never served after it
Invalidation runs through #[ObservedBy] observers with ShouldHandleEventsAfterCommit, and covers projects or tasks that change team
Uses Team::tasks() hasManyThrough plus #[Scope] attribute scopes, and the withCount alias for top projects is clean Eloquent
A renderable ExchangeRatesUnavailable exception keeps the controller to one line; the lock has a double-check, a failure cooldown and a long-lived last-known copy
The saving observer keeps completed_at in step with status (probe: it still holds inside DB::transaction)
Small and readable, with little ceremony

v.rationale: Both implementations pass their own suites (impl-2: 31 tests, impl-1: 43) and handle exchange rates almost the same way: a FormRequest that upper-cases and validates the code, a fresh read, then a blocking lock with a double-check, a 3s timeout, a failure cooldown, a last-known copy, and stale or 503 on failure. The difference is the dashboard, which is the focus area. impl-2 uses Cache::flexible with a versioned per-team key bumped by after-commit observers. That meets 'reflect changes within seconds, stale up to 5 min is fine' in a few lines. impl-1 builds its own lock, random version key and ':last' fallback. Readers block for up to 5s on every miss instead of getting stale data, and on a cold cache under contention each waiter runs the expensive build itself. impl-1 also adds unneeded session middleware to the api group and primitive constructor seams. Its UserObserver is a nice extra, but it misses users created straight into a team (probe confirmed). impl-1 has the better tests: datasets, a race test, and no real sleeps. impl-2's tests are sound but thinner, and one of them really blocks for 4s. Since the focus is idiomatic caching, impl-2's simpler, more idiomatic and more correct dashboard ranks it first.
